description: Software and Design and Artificial intelligence
summary:
**Interplanetary Survival Guide: Martian Map** is an interactive planetary analysis and EVA route-planning platform designed to improve astronaut safety during Mars surface exploration.

Unlike existing tools focused on global and regional visualization, our system provides localized walking-scale route planning by combining terrain hazards, environmental uncertainty, and astronaut life-support constraints.

The platform uses a TypeScript/React visualization interface and a C# (.NET 9) spherical routing engine. It divides selected Martian regions into a spherical grid using a planetary radius of 3,396.19 km and up to 6,400 cells. It integrates USGS SIM3292 geological units, tectonic structures, and missing-data uncertainty into a quantitative Danger Factor (DF).

Using this risk model, BFS, Dijkstra, and A* algorithms compare minimum-step and minimum-risk routes. A stochastic hazard simulator introduces unexpected obstacles, propagates residual risk to neighboring cells, and calculates alternative routes in real time.

By transforming planetary datasets into actionable navigation intelligence, the platform supports safer, more efficient, and higher-return future human Mars exploration.
details:
Interplanetary Survival Guide: Martian Map is an interactive planetary surface analysis and Extravehicular Activity (EVA) route-planning platform designed to support safer, higher-return human Marswalks. While existing orbital tools such as JPL’s Mars Trek provide global and regional visualization, they are not built for hyperlocalized, walking-scale surface excursions. Our system bridges that gap by transforming planetary geological and structural layers into a spherical risk grid that enables astronauts and mission planners to compare fastest versus safest routes and dynamically reroute around sudden surface hazards.

How It Works:
Users select a rectangular exploration zone on the Martian surface and discretize it into a custom grid of up to $80 \times 80$ cells ($6,400$ cells maximum) on a Mars spherical coordinate system ($r = 3,396.19\text{ km}$). For every cell, the C# backend queries full, unsimplified USGS Scientific Investigations Map 3292 (SIM3292) geology polygons (UnitDesc) at the cell midpoint and intersects tectonic structures (Interpreta) across the cell rectangle. These factors are combined with an explicit missing-data penalty ($U$) to compute a dimensionless Danger Factor ($DF = 1 + (45T + 35M + 20U)/100$). Using this risk surface, users place start ($A$) and end ($B$) waypoints and compare routes generated by BFS, Dijkstra, and $A^*$. Users can also place a traveler along the active path and trigger simulated hazard events—which mark the central event cell forbidden, propagate attenuated residual risk to immediate neighbor cells based on spherical cell area, and compute valid contingency detours in real time.

Benefits:
- Hyperlocalized EVA Decision Support: Translates macro orbital datasets into walking-scale traverse grids with cell-by-cell geological evidence inspection.
- Balanced Life-Support & Safety Trade-Offs: Enables crews to compare minimum-step paths (BFS) against minimum-risk weighted paths (Dijkstra and $A^*$) to weigh suit oxygen and power limits against terrain danger.
- Real-Time Contingency Rerouting: Simulates sudden hazards ahead of a moving traveler, isolating blocked cells and immediately recalculating safe alternative routes.
- Honest Uncertainty Transparency: Explicitly quantifies unmeasured local parameters (such as slope, temperature, radiation, weather, rock size, and soil strength) rather than masking missing measurements as zero risk.
- Deterministic Scenario Replay: Supports seeded event sequences (up to $50$ cumulative events) so mission planners can reproduce, audit, and stress-test identical traverse scenarios.

Intended Impact:
Interplanetary Survival Guide: Martian Map strengthens astronaut situational awareness and mission resilience during surface excursions by turning static planetary maps into an actionable tactical navigation engine. Beyond Mars, the platform is architected to scale into a planet-agnostic exploration engine: as long as planetary geology, structural hazard layers, and body radius/coordinate metadata are supplied in a standardized input file schema, the software can ingest the dataset, automatically plot the surface map for any planet or moon (such as the Moon under Artemis, Titan, or Europa), and deploy its full risk-scoring, pathfinding, and hazard-rerouting suite without core algorithm rewrites.

Development Tools and Technology Stack:
- Frontend & Visualization (TypeScript 82.0%, CSS 3.5%, HTML 0.7%, JavaScript 0.4%): Built with React, Vite, Tailwind CSS, and LightningCSS to render interactive map overlays, risk grids, traveler waypoints, and route comparisons through a local API proxy.
- Backend & Routing Engine (C# 6.5%): Powered by a .NET 9 ASP.NET Core REST API (Mars.Api.csproj) executing exact spatial polygon/rectangle queries, $DF$ risk calculations, BFS/Dijkstra/$A^*$ routing, and stochastic hazard simulations.
- GIS Data Pipeline & Verification (Python 6.9%): Offline Python utilities prepare USGS SIM3292 shapefiles and Robinson-to-Mars-sphere hillshade rasters ($1800 \times 900\text{ px}$), supported by automated C#, TypeScript (tsx), and Python API test suites.
- API Contract & Client Generation: Defined via an OpenAPI specification (openapi.yaml) that automatically generates a strongly typed React API client.
- Planetary Datasets: Driven by a 23-layer local snapshot of USGS Scientific Investigations Map 3292 (Global_Geology.shp, Global_Structure.shp, Global_Contacts.shp, Global_Landing_sites.shp, and reprojected hillshade imagery).

Creativity and Innovation:
Rather than treating missing planetary telemetry as safe ground, our model introduces an explicit Missing-Data Penalty ($U$) alongside a conservative worst-case overlap rule—ensuring overlapping geological units or tectonic structures always take the highest risk tier rather than being diluted by averaging. To keep the web interface fast without sacrificing analytical accuracy, we engineered a dual-geometry pipeline that renders $0.025^\circ$ simplified vectors in the browser while running full, unsimplified spatial intersections on the C# server. Additionally, our area-aware hazard propagation model attenuates peripheral risk across neighboring cells using true spherical surface area ($A$) and diagonal offset distance ($\sqrt{dr^2 + dc^2}$), while visually separating historical infeasible paths (dashed amber) from active detour routes (solid blue) as a traveler advances.

Design Considerations:
- Scientific Honesty & Transparency: Clearly separates derived proxy movement costs ($DF$) from real-world physical safety probabilities and keeps raw source evidence distinct from simulated events.
- Planetary Coordinate Hygiene: Strictly enforces Mars spherical coordinates ($r = 3,396,190\text{ m}$) and prevents silent mixing with Earth WGS84 or incompatible ellipsoid layers.
- Computational Efficiency: Caps grid generation at $6,400$ cells ($80 \times 80$) and decouples lightweight UI display GeoJSONs from exact backend geometry queries.
- Determinism & Auditability: Supports seeded random event sampling and full event-history replay from the clean baseline, validated against synthetic lab fixtures (POST /lab).
- Universal Extensibility: Structured around modular data contracts so future missions can plug in standardized planetary datasets for any moon or planet, alongside high-resolution DEMs, rover LiDAR, or live suit telemetry.

In essence, Interplanetary Survival Guide: Martian Map is more than a static planetary viewer—it is a modular, scientifically transparent EVA navigation and contingency-planning framework built to guide human explorers safely across Mars and future worlds beyond.
